We present LSeg (Language-driven Semantic Segmnetation), a model that can segment images into categories specified by natural language.

(1) LSeg is a novel model for semantic segmentation that uses a transformer-based image encoding to compute dense per-pixel representations of the input image and align them with text representations of the input labels, and (2) LSeg achieves competitive zero-shot and few-shot performance compared to traditional segmentation methods and other language-based approaches, and even matches accuracy when provided a fixed label set.
